### Front line

According to the Ukrainian open-source mapping project DeepStateMap, Russian forces newly occupied 8.6 square kilometers of previously contested territory, including portions of Lypivka (76%) and Nykyforivka (12%) in the Bakhmutskyi raion of Donetsk Oblast. 

Separately, the Russian Ministry of Defence claimed that its "Sever" (North) grouping took control of the settlements of Nefedovka and Chernoe in Kharkiv Oblast, asserting that it was tightening encirclement lines. The Russian defence ministry also claimed its forces struck Ukrainian positions with self-propelled artillery in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, while geolocated footage documented a Russian FPV drone strike on a claimed Ukrainian position in Stepnohirsk. In addition, geolocated imagery showed Russian defensive fortifications—including electronic warfare antennas, bunkers, machine gun positions, and anti-drone netting—installed on the roof of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP).

### Strikes and losses

Ukraine's Ministry of Defence claimed that Ukrainian Naval Forces struck the Borisoglebsk military airfield inside Russia with Neptune missiles, destroying four and damaging two Russian Su-34M bombers that were allegedly loaded with aerial bombs.

Conversely, the Russian Ministry of Defence claimed multiple successful strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure and logistics:
* Russian forces claimed long-range drone strikes damaged port infrastructure at Izmail and Yuzhny in Odesa Oblast, and that three dry-cargo vessels bound for Odesa were struck at sea and in port areas (including Black Sea approaches and Bugsky Liman). In contrast, open-source geolocated imagery recorded a Russian "Geran-4" drone striking a supermarket in Mayaky, Odesa Oblast, and a drone strike adjacent to a residential building that reportedly injured five civilians.
* Russian aviation and drone units claimed strikes on Ukrainian temporary deployment and drone control points in the areas of Bilozerske and Vysochoivanivka in Donetsk Oblast, as well as a fuel and lubricants depot and generator in Kramatorsk.
* Defensively, Russia's Ministry of Defence claimed that its air defences intercepted 166 Ukrainian drones overnight across multiple Russian regions, Crimea, and the Krasnodar region, and intercepted a further 80 drones during the day. It also claimed that Russian forces intercepted four long-range "Flamingo" cruise missiles and 69 drones targeting an oil refinery in Ryazan, conceding that falling drone debris caused a fire on the facility's grounds.

The Economist's war-fire model recorded six satellite fire detections classified as war-related, all located in Kirovohrad Oblast.

### Official statements

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence reported that Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara met with Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas to discuss long-term defence cooperation, with an emphasis on unmanned systems, electronic warfare, air defence interceptors, joint industrial production, and funding via the SAFE mechanism. The Ukrainian ministry also announced that 389 foreign defence companies have applied for access to its TrophyLab database, which details captured Russian military equipment. Additionally, it announced its first centralized procurement of 4,700 soft-armor fragmentation protective suits for frontline forces.

On the Russian side, Defence Minister Andrey Belousov attended a meeting of the Council of Defence Ministers of CIS Member States in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan. Russia and Kyrgyzstan signed a military cooperation plan for 2027, and Belousov highlighted joint efforts to integrate lessons and drone tactics from the war into collective operational training. Russian defence officials also announced the initial rollout of a unified digital military-medical system across several domestic military hospitals starting in December.
